137|### Build-and-Test failure loop-back (3.6 → 3.5)
138|
139|When Build and Test (3.6) diagnoses a failure whose ROOT CAUSE lies in the
140|generated code or an approach chosen at code-generation (not in this stage's
141|own test/build scaffolding), the workflow may return to code-generation and
142|repair it rather than writing the approach off or dead-ending at the gate.
143|The stage's Step 9 failure-escalation ladder decides WHEN this fires; this
144|subsection defines HOW. It is a sanctioned exception to the NO EMERGENT
145|BEHAVIOR RULE (like the revision escape hatch) and to Critical-checklist
146|item 5's "complete the current stage before jumping": a failed build-and-test
147|run is deliberately left in-flight — its gate is NOT presented and its enabled §13
148|learnings ritual DEFERS to the eventual passing run (when the `learnings` module is listed, the stage diary
149|memory.md persists across the loop; otherwise no diary or ritual runs).
150|
151|**The loop-back counter** lives in test-results.md under `## Loop-Back Log`:
152|the count of `### Loop-back N` entries IS the bound (max 3 per intent). This
153|artifact ledger is chosen over parsing STAGE_JUMPED audit rows because it
154|survives the backward jump (jumps reset checkboxes, never artifacts), is
155|colocated with the diagnosis it must carry anyway, and is readable at the
156|final gate; the STAGE_JUMPED rows the jump tool emits remain the
157|deterministic audit cross-check. The log is append-only. A human-directed
158|backward jump does not count against the bound — only entries this protocol
159|writes do.
160|
161|**Plan approval on replay.** The jump opens a new stage attempt, so the prior
162|Plan Approval receipt (bound to the previous attempt) cannot authorize the
163|replay. Preserve the
164|Loop-Back Log, but blank `[Answer]:`, regenerate the target-bound fingerprint,
165|and run Code Generation's Plan Approval decision/human-turn/answer receipt
166|sequence again before generation. The human's "Retry with fix" choice authorizes
167|the loop-back jump; it is not approval of plan content the human has not
168|reviewed under the new attempt.
169|
170|**Autonomous loop-back procedure** (mode `autonomous`, bound not exhausted,
171|impact-estimated fix identified):
172|1. Append the `### Loop-back N — <ISO timestamp>` entry (Diagnosis /
173|   Root-cause stage / Planned fix / Estimated impact) to test-results.md and a matching
174|   Deviations entry to this stage's memory.md.
175|2. Execute the jump through the ENGINE: run
176|   `bun .devin/tools/aidlc-orchestrate.ts next --stage code-generation`.
177|   The engine validates the target and answers with a `print` directive naming
178|   the exact `aidlc-jump.ts execute --target code-generation --direction
179|   backward --scope <scope>` command; run that printed command verbatim (it
180|   resets the target + downstream stages, emits the canonical `STAGE_JUMPED`,
181|   and pivots Current Stage), then re-run `next` and continue the forwarding
182|   loop. Never compose the `execute` call by hand — the engine's print is the
183|   validated form.
184|3. On the code-generation re-entry, follow "Re-entry settlement and review"
185|   below. Before any fix generation, run the fresh target-bound Plan Approval
186|   sequence required above; this is a human hard stop even though Construction
187|   autonomy remains granted. Then apply the planned fix ONLY to the unit(s) the diagnosis names and
188|   apply the deterministic Artifact Re-use decisions (see "Autonomous failure
189|   loop-back" under Artifact Re-use in stage-protocol.md). The standing
190|   `Construction Autonomy Mode: autonomous` grant is unchanged by the jump;
191|   after every applicable unit has a fresh current-attempt review, the replayed
192|   completion gate is auto-approved under it with
193|   `--user-input "Autonomous loop-back N per construction protocol module"` —
194|   the human already approved the original run of this stage; the replay is a
195|   repair of that approved shape, not a new autonomy inference (checklist item
196|   6).
197|4. Build and Test then re-runs naturally on the forward replay; choose Modify
198|   at its own Artifact Re-use prompt (never Redo — it would erase the
199|   Loop-Back Log) and re-execute Step 9 fresh.
200|
201|**Re-entry settlement and review.** Backward jumps preserve artifacts, but the
202|route depends on whether code-generation has ever used the unit lifecycle
203|ledger:
204|
205|1. **Artifact-only workflow** — when no code-generation lifecycle row has ever
206|   been emitted, artifacts remain the settlement signal. The re-entry `next`
207|   call can therefore emit the all-covered `gate: true` fast path. Apply the
208|   planned fix and the deterministic Modify/Keep decisions through the
209|   re-entry override BEFORE presenting or auto-approving that gate.
210|2. **Receipt-mode workflow** — once any code-generation lifecycle row exists,
211|   receipt mode is sticky. The jump invalidates the old attempt's settlement
212|   receipts, so re-entry emits per-unit `run-stage` directives. For each
213|   applicable unit, re-mint `unit start` / `unit complete`, applying the planned
214|   fix to targeted units and the deterministic **Modify targeted / Keep rest**
215|   Artifact Re-use decision inline as that unit re-runs.
216|
217|On BOTH paths, after every fix and re-use decision and BEFORE presenting or
218|auto-approving the settle/approval gate, dispatch code-generation's declared
219|reviewer for every applicable unit and record fresh current-attempt
220|`REVIEW_COMPLETED` receipts. The backward jump's `STAGE_JUMPED` invalidates
221|every prior review receipt, and the engine refuses approval while any applicable
222|unit lacks a fresh one. Under unit-major iteration the autonomous swarm never
223|fires: the replay follows the ordinary per-unit walk, re-mints lifecycle and
224|review receipts per unit as above, and the plan-approval carve-out keeps the
225|autonomous repair free of an extra human turn.
226|
227|**Swarm interaction.** On a loop-back replay where the engine emits
228|`invoke-swarm`, the jump establishes a new exact stage-attempt `Run floor`
229|boundary token (`<event>:<timestamp>#<ordinal>` over workflow start, jump,
230|rejection, and stage start boundaries). Each `SWARM_UNIT_CONVERGED` row must
231|match the current token, so prior-attempt rows no longer count and all units
232|re-dispatch by default. Before `prepare`, check for worktrees or
233|`bolt-<slug>` branches left by the prior attempt (a crash or a halt-and-ask
234|mid-swarm leaves them in place): `prepare` hard-errors on collision, and
235|`finalize` refuses a unit without the current attempt's prepare stamp, so
236|discard the stale worktrees/branches before a fresh `prepare` — never adopt
237|them into the new attempt. Do not spend a worker turn per unit: after
238|`prepare`, run
239|`check <unit> --check-cmd "<the project's convergence check>"` on every unit
240|FIRST. A unit already green needs no builder turn, but before putting it in
241|`finalize --claimed`, dispatch code-generation's reviewer in that fresh
242|worktree and record a terminal current-attempt `REVIEW_COMPLETED`. `finalize`
243|then verifies the current prepare stamp, the terminal receipt, and its current
244|artifact fingerprint before accepting the claim. Dispatch workers only for the
245|unit(s) the Loop-Back Log's planned fix targets or that fail the check, then
246|run the same reviewer pass after their final changes. The cheap path assumes
247|the prior attempt's code is in the base the worktrees forked from — true only
248|once that attempt's git code merge actually completed; if it did not (the
249|attempt halted before finalizing), every `check` comes back red and the cheap
250|path degrades gracefully to full re-dispatch rather than silently claiming
251|unbuilt units.
252|
253|**Halt-and-ask, impact-estimated variant (gated or unset mode, or bound exhausted, WITH
254|a candidate fix identified):**
255|
256|```question
257|prompt: "Build and Test failed: [short error]. Root cause: [diagnosis]. Candidate fix: [fix] — estimated impact — effort: [effort]; financial cost: [cost]; risk: [risk]. Loop-backs used: [N]/3. How would you like to proceed?"
258|header: Build Failure
259|multiSelect: false
260|options:
261|  - label: Retry with fix
262|    description: Jump back to code-generation, apply [fix] (estimated impact — effort: [effort]; financial cost: [cost]; risk: [risk]), re-run.
263|  - label: Accept failure
264|    description: Log the failure in test-results.md and proceed to this stage's approval gate.
265|  - label: Abort
266|    description: Stop here; the workflow can resume later.
267|```
268|
269|**Halt-and-ask, no-fix variant (no identifiable fix exists in any swappable
270|dimension):** omit "Retry with fix" entirely — presenting it without a
271|candidate fix would itself be the impact-unestimated give-up option this protocol
272|forbids in the other direction (a fabricated fix to retry with). Use:
273|
274|```question
275|prompt: "Build and Test failed: [short error]. Root cause: [diagnosis]. No identifiable fix exists in any swappable dimension (library/version, container image, instance type, algorithm, flag). Loop-backs used: [N]/3. How would you like to proceed?"
276|header: Build Failure
277|multiSelect: false
278|options:
279|  - label: Accept failure
280|    description: Log the failure in test-results.md and proceed to this stage's approval gate.
281|  - label: Abort
282|    description: Stop here; the workflow can resume later.
283|```
284|
285|Choose the variant by whether rung 2's classify-and-estimate step actually
286|produced an impact-estimated candidate fix — never render the impact-estimated template's
287|`Candidate fix` / `Retry with fix` slots with placeholder or invented
288|content just to keep the template shape.
289|
290|"Retry with fix" runs the same settlement-aware procedure as the autonomous
291|loop-back, including its re-entry override (see "Gated failure loop-back" under
292|Artifact Re-use in stage-protocol.md). Artifact-only workflows may take the
293|all-covered `gate: true` fast path; receipt-mode workflows instead re-emit
294|per-unit directives. On either path the planned fix and deterministic
295|Modify/Keep decisions MUST be applied BEFORE the settle/approval gate, and
296|every applicable unit MUST receive a fresh current-attempt review before that
297|gate is presented. A human-approved retry does count an entry in the Loop-Back
298|Log, and the human may override the bound explicitly. Every option's
299|description must carry its estimated impact where one is known — presenting an
300|impact-unestimated give-up option is a protocol violation.

  5|## 5. Multi-agent stages (ensemble topologies)
  6|
  7|Some stages use multiple agents (e.g., Feasibility uses aidlc-architect-agent + aidlc-aws-platform-agent + aidlc-compliance-agent). How the support agents participate is governed by the directive's `mode` — the stage's communication topology — never by the mere presence of `support_agents`. The roles are constant across topologies: the **lead agent** owns the stage's `produces[]` artifacts, **support agents** collaborate as real participants who write their own work, and the `reviewer` (stage-protocol-reviewer.md §12a, when declared) verifies from outside afterwards. The orchestrator is the bus on every topology: every exchange between participants is a dispatch it makes and a return it carries. Agents do NOT invoke each other — only the orchestrator delegates.
  8|
  9|**What the user hears while an ensemble runs.** These handoffs happen inside a stage, past the reach of a directive's `narration`, so the sentences are written here. Only the double-quoted text is spoken; fill the `[bracketed]` slots and drop the brackets.
 10|
 11|- Handing a specific question to one specialist - **SAY:** "Let me bring in the [trade] on [the specific question, in plain terms]."
 12|- Starting a chain where each specialist builds on the last - **SAY:** "The [first trade] takes a look first, then the [next trade] builds on what comes back."
 13|- Convening several specialists at once - **SAY:** "Getting the [trade] and [trade] to weigh in on this together."
 14|- A specialist's work has come back and you are folding it in - **SAY:** nothing. Integration is the work, not an event.
 15|
 16|Trades, never agent names, files, or slugs: product manager, product lead, designer, delivery lead, architect, architecture reviewer, platform engineer, compliance specialist, security engineer, developer, quality engineer, release engineer, operations engineer. Nothing is said about handing off as a mechanism, briefs, context paths, rule bundles, contribution files, identity markers, blindness between participants, rounds, or which topology the stage declares. The user is meeting colleagues; that setup is ours, not theirs. A topology that does not apply is never mentioned either.

 18|**Who writes what (mirrors a real working session — everyone writes; the owner collates and edits):**

 20|- Each dispatched support agent WRITES its own **contribution file** at `<record>/<phase>/<stage>/contributions/<agent-slug>.md` (per-unit stages: under the unit's stage dir). Separate files per agent, so parallel dispatch never conflicts. The file's FIRST line is the identity marker verbatim: `**Collaborator:** <agent-slug>`, followed by `## Contribution` (the substantive content, written to be integrable) and `## Positions` (`AGREE:` / `OBJECT:` bullets with one-line rationales; `None` = full agreement).
 21|- The LEAD integrates contributions into the stage's `produces[]` artifacts and owns their final state. Contribution files are part of the stage's permanent record — dissent stays on disk, not in ephemeral return text.
 22|- On `pipeline`, the chain collectively authors the artifacts directly (serialized, so no conflict) and the conductor mints a durable link receipt after every return — see the topology bullet.

 24|- **`mode: inline`** — the support agents are perspectives the orchestrator adopts in its own context: load each support agent's file + knowledge the same way you loaded the lead (see "For inline stages" above), produce the lead's output first, then layer in each support perspective, then synthesise. Do NOT dispatch a support agent on an inline stage; dispatch is reserved for the other modes. No contribution files.

If the stage declares `support_agents`, dispatch each one against the returned draft (artifacts by path per §11's context budget, rules as the accumulated steering bundle per "For subagent stages" above; spokes are mutually blind - no support agent's brief contains another's contribution); each spoke writes its contribution file; then dispatch the lead once more to integrate the contributions into the artifacts.

On entry or resume, skip every completed entry and dispatch the FIRST missing link. After each link returns, mint its receipt before dispatching the next: `bun .devin/tools/aidlc-log.ts link --stage "<directive.stage>" --link "<agent>"`. Each link sees everything upstream and advances the work product directly — it may edit the evolving artifacts in place (serialized, no conflict) or hand results down as context for the next link to build on, per the stage body. The FINAL link leaves the `produces[]` artifacts complete. Order is the point. No contribution files required.

  1|# Learnings Protocol Module
  2|
  3|Load this module when the directive lists `learnings` in `directive.protocol_modules`. It applies only while `directive.ceremony.learnings === "on"`.
  4|
  5|## 13. Learnings Ritual
  6|
  7|MANDATORY when this module is listed: Every stage that reaches a human approval gate runs the learnings-capture step **between the completion message (§2) and the approval gate (§1)**. The auto-proceeding bootstrap initialization stages and isolated `single: true` runs have no workflow approval gate and bypass this ritual; unfinished per-unit iterations defer it until the stage's one final gate. Per Fowler's harness model: "when issues recur, feedforward and feedback controls should be improved." This ritual is the human learning loop — surface what's worth remembering, write it into the harness where the next runner will pick it up automatically.
  8|
  9|The ritual is **tool-as-actor**: a deterministic tool (`aidlc-learnings.ts`) detects, surfaces, routes, and writes; the orchestrator-LLM renders the structured question and runs the admission conflict-check; the user decides keep / heading / scope. Detection, surfacing, routing, and writing are all deterministic; judgement is the user's.
 10|
 11|### What changes vs what doesn't
 12|
 13|**Stage files are immutable framework artefacts.** The ritual NEVER edits a stage file's `## Steps`, `## Sensors`, or `## Learn` content. Stage files ship with framework releases; user-tier customisation lives in the harness. The one carve-out is the frontmatter `sensors:` import list — a sensor-binding addition appends a new id there (the pull-authoring two-write install). That is the import list, not body content; the stage's immutable shape is unchanged. Stage files are framework-and-loop-edited, not framework-only — but only that one frontmatter list grows.
 14|
 15|**The harness IS mutable.** A confirmed learning IS a practice — it writes to one of two surfaces:
 16|
 17|- `aidlc/spaces/<space>/memory/project.md` (default) or `aidlc/spaces/<space>/memory/team.md` — appended as a practice line under the fitting topical heading (e.g. `## Corrections`, `## Testing Posture`, `## Forbidden`), one click to widen a candidate from project to team. These are the SAME method files the resolver reads; there is no parallel `*-learnings.md` surface, no fractional override tier, and no org tier (no widen-to-org path). History of what was learned lives in the audit shards + the per-stage diary, not a rolling dated file.
 18|- `.devin/sensors/aidlc-<id>.md` — for verification checks. A project-tier manifest with a `matches:` capability glob, bound to the originating stage by appending its id to that stage's `sensors:` frontmatter list.
 19|
 20|Next time the stage runs, the resolved rules and the bound sensor load automatically at compile — the stage runs better without anyone having edited the stage file's body.
 21|
 22|### When to run
 23|
 24|The current directive controls applicability even if this module was loaded earlier in the session. When it is no longer listed, keep no diary and skip the ritual.
 25|
 26|When this module is listed, trigger after Step N-1 (completion message rendered) and before Step N (approval gate), only when the engine emits the stage's actual human gate. A `gate: false` iteration does not run the ritual. Bootstrap initialization stages keep only the diary (step 1), with no surfacing, question, admission, or persistence. Isolated `single: true` runs keep no diary and run none of this module. Per-unit `gate: false` iterations keep their diary and defer the ritual to the stage's final gate. Team-owned unit-major gates are the exception: run the ritual at each emitted `directive.unit_gate`, with the matching Unit identity, rather than waiting for the solo final stage gate. Gate revisions never rerun the ritual; re-present the approval gate directly.
 27|
 28|### The ritual
 29|
 30|1. **Maintain a per-stage memory file as you work.** Append entries to `<record>/<phase>/<stage>/memory.md` (created by the engine from the shipped template when it emits the run-stage directive, only when the learnings ritual is on). Treat this path as an output-only target: the orchestrator never reads, probes, creates, or initializes it, and follows the active harness's diary-write discipline when inserting entries. Use four standard H2 headings:
 31|   - **Interpretations** — choices made where the stage prose was ambiguous
 32|   - **Deviations** — places where you intentionally departed from the stage prose, and why
 33|   - **Tradeoffs** — alternatives considered and why you picked what you did
 34|   - **Open questions** — anything to confirm before next run, or uncertain context worth flagging
 35|
 36|   Each entry is a bullet under the appropriate heading with an ISO 8601 timestamp prefix:
 37|   ```markdown
 38|   - 2026-05-20T10:14:32Z — <one-line summary>; <2-3 sentences of context>
 39|   ```
 40|
 41|   The memory file persists across sessions — a stage that halts and resumes keeps its log intact. On stage approval, the memory file stays in the artefact directory as part of the stage's permanent record (committed alongside other artefacts).
 42|
 43|2. **Surface candidates (the tool reads memory.md).** Run:
 44|   ```bash
 45|   bun .devin/tools/aidlc.ts engine learnings surface --slug <stage-slug>
 46|   ```
 47|   The tool parses memory.md and emits structured JSON: one candidate per non-blank entry under **Interpretations / Deviations / Tradeoffs** (surfaced verbatim — no paraphrase, no "interesting" filtering), plus a read-only `parked_open_questions[]` list. Open questions are research items, not learnings to install — they never become candidates. Most runs surface nothing worth keeping; that's the most common outcome. The output also carries `space` and `intent` — the workspace's active space/intent resolved AT THIS MOMENT, not re-derived later. Carry both verbatim into the selections file in step 5; `persist` uses these, never the live active-intent cursor, so a later intent switch before persisting can't misattribute the write. Multiple intent records with no valid active-intent cursor is a hard failure here, not a silent `intent: null`.
 48|
 49|3. **Render the structured question + free-text channel.** For each candidate, render one option whose `label` is the candidate `summary` (verbatim) and whose `description` names the routed destination (e.g. `→ project.md ## Corrections`) plus a "promote to team?" affordance. After `multiSelect` returns, correlate each kept label back to its candidate `id` + `source_heading`. Then **always** ask the human "Anything to add for next time?" with at least two explicit choices: **Nothing to add** and **Add a note**. This question is mandatory even when `surface` returned zero candidates: do not infer or self-select **Nothing to add**, and END YOUR TURN at the question — the approval gate is a separate, later turn, never rendered in the same message. This is a structured question, so the §3 logging pair applies to it like any other: `aidlc-log.ts decision` before presenting it, `aidlc-log.ts answer` with the human's exact choice after — the resulting `QUESTION_ANSWERED` row preceding the gate's `STAGE_AWAITING_APPROVAL` is the auditable proof the ritual ran as its own human interaction. `Add a note` opens a free-text follow-up; a harness-provided Other/notes escape remains a direct free-text path. Never emit a one-option structured question — Claude Code and Codex reject it. For any non-empty response, ask the user to pick one of the four diary headings (Interpretation / Deviation / Tradeoff / Open question). **The diary-heading pick is the only classification asked of the user.** From it, the orchestrator routes the learning to the fitting practice heading in the method file (KNOWLEDGE): a testing learning → `## Testing Posture`, a prohibition → `## Forbidden`, anything general → `## Corrections` (the default). The user never picks the destination heading directly — the orchestrator routes by fit, and the tool ensure-exists the heading before it writes.
 50|
 51|4. **Admission conflict-check (before any write).** For each kept learning candidate, compare the proposed practice line against `org.md`'s matching `## <section>` (matched by the routed heading — the single-line variant of the §5 admission gate). This comparison is a section-level LLM check (knowledge → orchestrator-LLM). If the practice contradicts an org guardrail, surface the conflicting org sentence inline; the user **revises, skips this candidate, or escalates** (judgement → user; there is no user-override path). Only conflict-clear or user-escalated selections proceed to the write. Sensor manifests have no org-section analogue and skip this check.
 52|
 53|5. **Persist (the tool writes + emits audit).** Build the selections file — `{ stage_slug, space, intent, selections[] }`, where `space`/`intent` are carried verbatim from step 2's surface output — and call:
 54|   ```bash
 55|   bun .devin/tools/aidlc.ts engine learnings persist --slug <stage-slug> --selections-json <path>
 56|   ```
 57|   The tool rejects a `--slug` that differs from the selections file's `stage_slug`, then verifies inside one `withAuditLock` transaction that the pinned space and non-null intent record still exist. It deduplicates against both the fresh audit snapshot and hashes emitted earlier in the same batch, using a `<!-- cid:<intent-slug>:<stage-slug>:<content-hash> -->` marker whose content hash is the full SHA-256 digest of the learning text. A crashed run therefore recovers without double-appending, while distinct learning text cannot share a truncated persisted identity:
 58|   - **Learning** → appends a practice line under the orchestrator-routed heading in `<scope>.md` (scope ∈ {project, team}): `- <text> (learned YYYY-MM-DD) <!-- cid:... -->`. Ensure-exists the heading first, so a routed heading the file doesn't yet carry is created rather than throwing. Emits `RULE_LEARNED` (with `Source: orchestrator | user_addition`, `Heading: <routed>`).
 59|   - **Sensor** → scaffolds a project-tier `<project>/.devin/sensors/aidlc-<id>.md` manifest (with the user-supplied `matches:` glob) AND appends the new id to the originating stage's `sensors:` frontmatter list — both writes inside the same lock. Emits `SENSOR_PROPOSED`. The sensor binds and fires from the next workflow's compile.
 60|
 61|   The orchestrator never `Edit`s a rule or sensor file directly — every learning write goes through the tool under the lock, so the `RULE_LEARNED` / `SENSOR_PROPOSED` audit row is the replayable source of truth for what was learned. The selections file is the replay artefact: a crashed persist replays the same selections-json without re-prompting the human.
 62|
 63|6. **Proceed to approval gate.** The ritual is advisory and additive — it never blocks the gate after the human responds. If the user skipped all candidates and explicitly chose **Nothing to add**, proceed directly; zero surfaced candidates alone is not permission to skip the mandatory question in step 3.
 64|
 65|### Routing decision tree
 66|
 67|```
 68|Is the entry an Interpretation / Deviation / Tradeoff?
 69|└── Learning → a practice line under the routed heading in <scope>.md
 70|    Heading routed by fit (testing → ## Testing Posture, prohibition →
 71|      ## Forbidden, general → ## Corrections); ensure-exists before write.
 72|    Scope derived from the user's keep + optional promote:
 73|    ├── default                       — project.md
 74|    └── promote scope (project→team)  — team.md   (no org tier)
 75|
 76|Is the entry an Open question?
 77|└── Parked — research item, never installed.
 78|
 79|Is the improvement a verification check?
 80|└── Sensor (two-write install): scaffold a project-tier manifest at
 81|    .devin/sensors/aidlc-<id>.md with a matches: glob, AND append its id to
 82|    the originating stage's sensors: frontmatter list (one locked transaction).
 83|    The matches: glob is a capability filter — stages: [<id>] is the binding.
 84|```
 85|
 86|### What goes where — quick reference
 87|
 88|| Entry shape | Destination |
 89||---|---|
 90|| Interpretation: "Reused the auth module rather than rewriting it" | `project.md ## Corrections` (practice line, `(learned YYYY-MM-DD)`) |
 91|| Deviation: "Used Given/When/Then for AC despite freeform prose" | `project.md ## Testing Posture` (practice line); promote to `team.md` if team-wide |
 92|| Tradeoff: "Picked TDD over BDD for the new generators this run" | `project.md ## Testing Posture` (practice line) |
 93|| Open question: "Confirm whether story splitting is by persona or journey" | Parked — never installed |
 94|| Check: "ADRs should carry Security and Compliance headings" | Sensor manifest `aidlc-<id>.md` (`matches:` glob) bound to the stage via its `sensors:` frontmatter |
 95|
 96|### Why stage files stay immutable
 97|
 98|Two reasons: (1) framework upgrades to a stage file would conflict with workflow-time edits; (2) the same stage runs in many projects, so stage-file body mutations would mean every workflow drifts the framework's methodology in incompatible directions. The harness layer (rules, learnings, sensors) is designed to compose — many small additions accumulate without conflicts. Stage-file bodies are not. The sensor-binding frontmatter edit is the one sanctioned exception: it grows the `sensors:` import list (immutable in shape, not in contents), never the `## Steps` / `## Sensors` / `## Learn` body.

  13|shipping their work. So narrate the work, not the plumbing. "I'm working out
  14|which parts of the development process fit this change" lands; "the
  15|orchestration engine is resolving the compiled scope grid" does not.
  16|

  18|for chat narration:** engine, directive, dispatch, conductor, harness, verb,
  19|scope grid, steering, forwarding loop, mint, swarm, entropy, and the
  20|ARS component names (IAE, CSU, VE, R, UA). The user's project has none of
  21|these things.

  24|

  28|| the next directive | the next step |
  29|| dispatch the architect agent | hand this off to the architect, or bring in the architect |
  30|| your harness / the harness dir | your project setup |
  31|| mint an intent | create a workflow or record |
  32|| verify / validate the artifact | check it |

  36|user should look at, and what happens after they approve. Name files by path

  41|then the FIRST sentence is plain language; the specifics follow it.

  43|**When an action is refused, translate the refusal instead of relaying it.**
  44|The tool, hook, or workflow check's own message is diagnostic output, not chat
  45|narration: never quote or paraphrase its internal vocabulary to the user. Say
  46|one plain sentence naming what was declined and why in the user's project
  47|terms, then one plain sentence naming the next step they can take. For example:
  48|"I can't edit the stories document right now because it was already reviewed
  49|for approval. To change it, you can request changes and I'll revise and

  75|problem was never the vocabulary: the user has no iteration and no gate

What happened, in project terms: the earlier session approved the plan, this session re-approved it cleanly (the approval was recorded successfully), but the handoff check that lets me bring in the developer still reports the plan as not currently approved. `/aidlc --doctor` shows no blocking problems — only advisories (hook PATH for bun, uncommitted `aidlc/` records, plugin sync).

A couple of options for how to proceed:

- Restart Devin CLI and run `/aidlc --resume` — the approval is durably recorded, so a fresh session may clear whatever stale check is blocking the handoff.
- Or, if you'd rather, I can try running this tiny stage's work directly in this session (it's just `hello.py` plus a small `test_hello.py`) — though the workflow's guard may require the delegated path to count it as complete.

Which would you like?
